headline: High: shared git workspace plus broad shell/network access creates dangerous write-conflict and prompt-to-action pathways; compliance risk is lower but nonzero.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Aider can read/write repo files and uses stdin/stdout plus shared git state; plano can consume config/files and send chat completions. If Aider writes attacker-controlled text into tracked files, plano may ingest it as instructions. No direct shared clipboard/MCP is shown, so this is not high.
conditions: IF Aider writes untrusted content into a repo file that plano later reads
IF plano treats file or log content as instruction-bearing input
mitigations: Review repo files before plano reads them
Separate prompt-bearing files from code files
Add a fixed instruction prefix in plano
Use a throwaway branch for Aider edits
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between tools

B_data_leakage.rationale: Aider touches source code and git history, while plano touches logs, traces, metrics, and config. A shared repo or workspace can expose code or history to plano, and plano’s broad egress can transmit that context to its backend. The profiles do not prove a default shared filesystem, so medium is the higher safe choice.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or repo
IF plano forwards file-derived context into its chat-completions backend
mitigations: Redact secrets from repo history before use

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Aider has unrestricted filesystem write and modify_git_state, and its shared_state_with_other_instances is via a shared git repo. Plano can also read files and has broad network egress. Concurrent edits to the same repo can race and corrupt git state or overwrite each other; the shared mutable surface is explicit, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git repository
IF plano writes config or generated artifacts while Aider commits edits
mitigations: Run only one writer at a time
Lock the repo during plano writes

D_cascading_error.rationale: Aider produces code changes and git commits; plano can consume files and emit routed chat-completion outputs. If plano treats Aider’s edits or generated text as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream actions or bad routing decisions. The profiles do not show explicit verification, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF plano uses Aider-produced files as authoritative input
IF plano routes or acts on outputs without a verification step
mitigations: Require human review of Aider diffs
Add schema validation before plano consumes outputs

E_compliance.rationale: Aider is open-source and documents model-provider API keys via env vars; plano is open-source but unverified and touches logs/metrics/traces. No explicit residency or regulated-data mismatch is shown, so only a small compliance gap is visible. The other agent is cited because the risk is about their combined handling of the same operational data.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into plano logs or traces
IF Aider repo contents include secrets or personal data
mitigations: requires-engineering: align residency and retention policies
